learn.hook: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time on a number line: 3, 6, 9, 12... Will it ever land on 20?
points: Jumping in equal steps from 0 lands on multiples: jumps of 4 land on 4, 8, 12, 16, 20...
A number is reached by a jump if it is a multiple of the jump size: 20 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 5) but not of 3.
The number of jumps to reach a target is target ÷ jump size: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 jumps.
The smallest 3-digit number reached by jumps of 8 is 104 (8 × 13).
Bigger jumps reach a number in fewer jumps: to reach 24, a 3-jumper needs 8 jumps, an 8-jumper needs only 3.

points: A common multiple is a number that is a multiple of both jump sizes.
